## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #17624 

Reference to `ChangeDetectorRef` is not freed on `ngOnDestroy` leading to bigger memory leak (eg. there might be still detached DOM nodes in ViewRef that cannot be garbage collected).

## What is the new behavior?

This is interim fix. Still waiting for final fix in ReactiveX/rxjs#2675
On disposing of async pipe, the reference to `ChangeDetectorRef` is cleared, so garbage collector can free more memory.

issue.title: Get rid of RxJs
issue.body:
## I'm submitting a... 

[ ] Regression (a behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[ ] Bug report  
[x] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
## Current behavior Please take a look at this expression and try to explain why it leads to memory leak: this.store.select(gT).filter(n => n.status=='status').take(1).subscribe(n => console.log(n) );
This expression leads to memory leaks because of unclosed subscribers when 'filter' returns false and there are a lot of cases such this. I don't want to double care about my memory, JavaScript cares about it. This is not native angular, but this is ngrx extension, which, I believe, was implemented because of Angular have started using Rx under the hood. ## Expected behavior Angular get rid of RxJs. (Replace to promises in native API?) ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? I hope that there is the way to control backpressure and combine streams with smallest and simplest library than rx.

body:
Using angular6, I can't reproduce the issue. It seems there is a memory leak in the shareReplay operator of rxjs 6 (and probably former versions), tracked there: https://github.com/ReactiveX/rxjs/issues/3336. 

This stackblitz may provide some insight: https://angular-kyver2.stackblitz.io

* The route A uses the shareReplay operator and subscribes using the aync pipe. Instances of this component are never garbage collected.
* The route B (un)subscribes manually using lifecycle hooks and avoid using the shareReplay operator. Instances are garbage collected.
* The route C does not use any share/shareReplay operator and subscribes using the async pipe. I don't understand the behaviour for this one, but it seems that both subscribers are able to receive the emitted values and that the component is correctly garbage collected.
* The route D uses the share operator and subscribes using the async pipe. Instances are correctly garbage collected.
* The route E uses the publishReplay + refcount operators as an alternative to the shareReplay operator and subscribes using the async pipe. Instances are correctly garbage collected.

@cghislai - I could not access your Stackblitz. It would be great if you could recreate it as a useful test environment for this issue.

It looks to me like this is really an upstream issue with RxJS usage - i.e. if you use certain kinds of RxJS operators on observables that you pass to `async` pipe you can get memory leaks.

That being said, it also seems that it would be prudent to apply the fix proposed by @czterocyty in https://github.com/czterocyty/angular/commit/928fd3ee7004f4edb4c0b20bade270571b30c751, which ensures that that `async` pipe is disconnected from the change detector when it is destroyed.

We could really do with a solid reproduction of the memory leak to allow us to test this.

@petebacondarwin indeed, it is by using the shareReplay operator that we obtain memory leak. The issue has been addressed upstream by the addition of a `refCount` paramter flag, see https://github.com/ReactiveX/rxjs/pull/4059. Using this parameter, the shareReplay operator will unsubscribe from its upstream observable when there are no longer any downstream subscription, allowing the angular component to be garbage collected. Ive nevertheless recreated the stackblitz at https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-risiq3 In the heap dump, it seems the async pipe is keeping a reference to the component through its change detector `_ref`, so the fix you mentioned might be worth testing. Im relinking the rejected mr https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/17629. Im not sure it is a proper solution neither, but it may indeed allow the components to be garbage collected and limit the impact of the memleak. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12647398/90054942-e0c2cc80-dcdc-11ea-874e-bb22dd96f94e.png) [Heap-20200812T204631.heapsnapshot.zip](https://github.com/angular/angular/files/5065002/Heap-20200812T204631.heapsnapshot.zip)
